title: Marathon Mathematics
claims: The analysis used Chicago Marathon data from 2005 to 2016.
Average finish times were 242 minutes for even splitters, 256 minutes for negative splitters and 280 minutes for positive splitters.
The fastest runners showed pace variation of less than 5% between the first and second half.
The wall was defined as slowing by at least 33% in the second half of the race.
Half of the runners who hit the wall ran their first 5 km as their fastest segment; those whose opening 5 km was their slowest never hit the wall and finished an average of 50 minutes faster.
About five times more runners ran even splits when running with or near a pacing group.
Male runners were 3 to 4 times more likely to hit the wall than women.
Women were better at producing even splits than men for a given finish time beyond 150 minutes.

claimVerification.note: 正文：使用 2005–2016 年芝加哥马拉松数据。
正文：匀速/负分段/正分段平均完赛时间 242/256/280 分钟。
正文：最快跑者前后半程配速变异小于 5%。
正文：撞墙定义为后半程减速至少 33%。
正文：撞墙者中 50% 首个 5 km 最快；首个 5 km 最慢者从不撞墙，平均快 50 分钟。
正文：跟随或靠近配速组时，匀速跑者约多 5 倍。
正文：男性撞墙概率为女性的 3–4 倍。
正文：完赛时间超过 150 分钟后，女性比男性更擅长匀速。

verification.note: 正文可读；8 条数字均见正文。
